hints.content:
The number lines show that the ratio of $\maroonD{\text{people}}$ to $\blueE{\text{percentage}}$ is $\maroonD{42}:\blueE{100\%}$.

We are looking for ratios that are equivalent to $\maroonD{42}:\blueE{100\%}$.

$\blueE{100}\div\blueE{50} = \purpleE{2}$

So. we can find the people for $\blueE{50\%}$ by dividing both parts of the ratio by $\purpleE{2}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So $\blueE{50\%}$ of $\maroonD{42}$ is $\maroonD{21}$.

options.alt: A double number line with 3 equally spaced tick marks. The line labeled People, reads from left to right: 0, 21, 42. The line labeled Percentage, reads from left to right: 0 percent, 50 percent, 100 percent. An arrow from the pair 42 to 100 percent to the pair 21 to 50 percent is labeled divided by 2.

hints.content:
Now we can find the people for $\blueE{150\%}$ by multiplying both parts of the new ratio by $\purpleE{3}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So $\blueE{150\%}$ of $\maroonD{42}$ is $\maroonD{63}$.

This makes sense because $\blueE{150\%}$ is more than $\blueE{100\%}$. So it should represent more than $\maroonD{42}$ people.

options.alt: A double number line with 4 equally spaced tick marks. The line labeled People, reads from left to right: 0, 21, 42, 63. The line labeled Percentage, reads from left to right: 0 percent, 50 percent, 100 percent, 150 percent. An arrow from the pair 21 to 50 percent to the pair 63 to 150 percent is labeled times 3.
